newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat to visit Egypt's Mubarak on peace crisis.
newsitem.headline: Arafat to visit Egypt's Mubarak on peace crisis.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat will travel to Cairo for talks with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on a peace crisis over a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem, an aide said on Wednesday.
"Arafat will go to Cairo on Thursday in order to coordinate with President Mubarak on the new situation," Arafat's aide Nabil Abu Rdainah said.
Israel broke ground on Tuesday for 6,500 homes for Jews on Jabal Abu Ghneim, a pine-covered hill occupied in 1967, prompting fears of violence. The hill is known as Har Homa in Hebrew.
Mubarak on Wednesday blasted the start of construction at the site.
"If this settlement is built this will not be the end of the whole thing. It will be the beginning of a new era of violence which we would like to avoid," he said in Cairo.

Israel's decision to build the settlement on land between Jerusalem and Bethlehem -- an area captured in the 1967 Middle East war -- was a blow to the Palestinians, who regard Arab East Jerusalem as the capital of a future state and say the construction precludes planned talks on the city's status.
Israel says all of Jerusalem is its "eternal" capital.
